Subject: Swiss processing carveout and transfer controls — initial scope

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo last week. Solaris is looking at a pilot that will contain Swiss patient records and our InfoSec/privacy team has asked us to confirm the options for keeping processing within Switzerland (or otherwise applying controls to avoid cross-border risk). Specific asks from procurement/legal:

- What transfer mechanisms would Redwood rely on for EU->CH and CH->US transit (SCCs, UK IDTA where relevant, plus DTIA/TIA mapping)?
- Can Redwood support a Swiss-only processing option (dedicated capacity in CH region or on-prem pattern)? If not, what compensating controls (proxying, encryption, KMS retention) do you recommend?
- Current subprocessors: please share the latest roster and indicate which subprocessors would touch decrypted content / KV cache.
- For our audit: SOC 2 report, KMS/HSM attestations, and sample audit log demonstrating residency controls.

Attached a high-level scope of the pilot (Solaris_Scope.pdf).

We are on a tight timeline and procurement would like a mutual action plan and a signing path (DocuSign or email). Can your team propose a short checklist and an initial timeline today or tomorrow?

Appreciate it — Sabine

--
Sabine Müller
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Solaris Health

Subject: Re: Swiss processing carveout and transfer controls — initial scope

Hi Sabine — thanks for the clear scope and the PDF.

Short answers up front:
1) Transfer mechanisms: For EU->CH we typically rely on SCCs supplemented by a DTIA/TIA mapping for technical/operational controls. If the legal team requires UK IDTA coverage for UK subjects we will include the UK Addendum. For CH-specific residual risk, we classify the flow as ‘onshore-equivalent’ when processing stays on dedicated CH capacity.

2) Swiss-only option: Redwood can provision Dedicated CH capacity (reserved VMs / GPU pools deployed in our Zurich region partner). That pattern keeps plaintext and KV caches within CH. Alternative is a Private deployment (VPC) — both require a purchase order and an implementation sprint (2–4 weeks) depending on provisioning windows.

3) Subprocessors: Attached is our current roster and a short matrix that flags which subprocessors access decrypted content. See Redwood_SCC-UKIDTA-TIA-Checklist.xlsx for the mapping and our recommended technical mitigations (prefix caching disabled, HSM-wrapped KMS keys for CH keys).

4) Audit artifacts: SOC 2 and HSM/KMS attestation can be provided under NDA; we have a SOC 2 Type II report currently valid through 2028.

Next steps I recommend:
- We (Redwood) provide a one-page Mutual Action Plan for the Solaris pilot with milestones: procurement signoff, PO for Dedicated CH capacity (if chosen), deployment window, security evidence handoff, go/no-go.
- Legal redline window: 3 business days after we issue the DPA + UK Addendum (if needed).
- Call: propose Mon 28 Jun 09:00 CEST / 08:00 BST or Mon 28 Jun 11:00 CEST for a 30-min run-through (Jonas and Marissa are on copy).

I attached a short one-pager summarizing the CH Dedicated option (Redwood_Swiss_Option_Summary.pdf) and the checklist workbook referenced above.

If that works I’ll draft the MAP and a DocuSign envelope with the DPA + UK Addendum + optional DTIA statement.

Best,
Kimberly

Kim — quick notes from Legal:
- We should propose the DPA + standard SCCs as the baseline. Add the UK IDTA only if Solaris confirms UK subjects in the data set.
- For the Swiss-only ask, include an acceptance clause: Solaris will sign a PO for Dedicated CH capacity and acknowledge the 2–4 week provisioning lead time.
- Ask Procurement for any billing constraints (e.g., whether the PO must be monthly commit vs one-time setup fee).

Also Sabine — could you confirm whether Solaris requires a vendor attestation that no US-based subprocessors will have access to plaintext when CH Dedicated is used? If so we will add the subprocessor isolation language and a technical attestation (HSM-wrapped CH KMS keys, dedicated Egress ACLs).

Marissa
